name: Leon Trotsky
description: Revolutionary socialist assessed through his opposition to Stalinist bureaucracy and advocacy of international revolution.

axes.brief: He demands genuine Soviet elections, criticism and accountable workers’ representatives against bureaucratic rule.
axes.counterEvidence: He allows Soviet parties rather than unrestricted capitalist restoration and historically excludes exploiting classes; earlier civil-war coercion is retained as counter-evidence.

qualifications.5: Restoring competing Soviet parties supports opposition within the socialist framework; equal conditions for every anti-socialist party are stronger than the proposal.

axes.brief: Exile writings defend criticism, cultural freedom and workers’ initiative against police bureaucracy while retaining revolutionary defensive coercion.
axes.counterEvidence: His earlier defence of terror and coercive labour cannot be erased; opposition to Stalin’s repression is not a complete liberal rights doctrine.

qualifications.16: Revolutionary security and opposition to arbitrary bureaucratic repression provide conflicting indications.

axes.brief: International working-class solidarity and national self-determination allow distinct cultures while favouring common socialist civic participation.
axes.counterEvidence: Changing inherited life and patriarchal culture qualifies treating every tradition as immune from socialist reform.

qualifications.9: Common socialist institutions and several national cultures can coexist without a single universal calendar.

axes.brief: Exile experience and international labour solidarity suggest broad lawful movement and refuge without cultural or class exclusion of workers.
axes.counterEvidence: Modern visa and welfare mechanisms are analogical; international revolution does not itself demonstrate abolishing every border institution.

axes.brief: He supports defending the workers’ state and revolutionary military capability while opposing imperialist wars and bureaucratic adventurism.
axes.counterEvidence: Revolutionary anti-war politics are not pacifism; military force remains a tool under class and defensive purposes.

qualifications.14: Revolutionary defence and avoiding futile escalation can conflict.

axes.brief: Revolutionary internationalism and a worldwide socialist federation take precedence over isolated national socialism.
axes.counterEvidence: Existing bourgeois international bodies are not equivalent to a democratically organised workers’ federation; modern court answers are conditional analogies.

axes.brief: He defends nationalised production and democratic control by producers and consumers.
axes.counterEvidence: He criticised bureaucratic administration and retained accounting rather than calling for capitalist ownership; ownership and managerial initiative are distinct.

axes.brief: A workers’ state protects a planned economy from capitalist restoration while seeking international economic cooperation under socialist transformation.
axes.counterEvidence: Internationalism does not imply unrestricted private foreign ownership or an unregulated capitalist trade market.

axes.brief: He advocates a democratically revised economic plan with public control of investment and distribution and transparent monetary accounting.
axes.counterEvidence: Factory initiative and meaningful accounting qualify rigid bureaucratic schedules for every wage or decision.

qualifications.7: Workers’ initiative and coordinated investment conflict under entirely unrestricted industry entry.

axes.brief: His programme seeks socialist equality and abolition of bureaucratic privilege, while recognising necessary transitional earnings differences.
axes.counterEvidence: Ultimate equality is not an assertion that every transitional worker is already paid identically; compensated land redistribution is a milder modern analogue.

axes.brief: Materialist socialist politics reject clerical control and religious foundations of state policy.
axes.counterEvidence: Atheism alone is not the basis for the scores: civil secular institutions and cultural emancipation in the writings supply the context.

axes.brief: He opposes patriarchal family constraints and Stalin’s rollback of reproductive and social emancipation.
axes.counterEvidence: Modern marriage and gender-identity mechanisms were not all explicitly discussed; progressive socialist transformation is contextual evidence rather than a documented contemporary questionnaire.

axes.brief: Scientific development and deliberate improvement of material life are central to his account of socialist culture.
axes.counterEvidence: Actual medical technologies were unknown to him; respect for scientific investigation qualifies reckless adoption without any evidence.

qualifications.4: Scientific caution and transformative ambition conflict under a long-term proof requirement.
qualifications.14: Productive improvement and serious ecological uncertainty give opposing considerations.

axes.brief: Soviet recall and national self-determination coexist with coordinated socialist economic planning.
axes.counterEvidence: Local democratic participation differs from autonomous capitalist local policy; world federation need not entail one unaccountable central administration.

axes.brief: His new-everyday-life writing emphasises social education, transformed habits and cultural learning alongside material and biological conditions.
axes.counterEvidence: Historical materialism is not a quantitative claim about each inherited psychological trait; the record supports qualified estimates, not automatic culture-pole answers.

sources.title: Cultural debates and political struggle in 1923 — research abstract

religion.reason: His adult atheism is explicitly identified in the biographical record, distinct from Jewish family origin.
